articles.title: ¿Junior vs. Real Madrid?: La millonaria y sorpresiva propuesta que le lanzaron a Florentino Pérez
articles.standfirst: ¿El Real Madrid en el nuevo Metropolitano? La propuesta a Florentino Pérez que ilusiona al Junior
articles.summary: ¿El Real Madrid en el nuevo Metropolitano? La propuesta a Florentino Pérez que ilusiona al Junior
articles.body: La posibilidad de ver al Real Madrid en Barranquilla dejó de ser solo una fantasía futbolera. Mauricio Gómez, ministro de Comercio, reveló que planteó a Florentino Pérez, presidente del club español, un amistoso entre el conjunto blanco y Junior de Barranquilla en el renovado estadio de la capital del Atlántico. La idea no contempla únicamente un partido en Colombia. Según Gómez, Pérez respondió que, si el proyecto se concreta, debería organizarse mediante dos encuentros: uno en Barranquilla y otro en Madrid. “Le planteé a Florentino un duelo con el Junior en el nuevo estadio. Le dije: hermano, tenemos un nuevo estadio. Entonces queremos ver al Junior de Barranquilla con el Real Madrid”, relató el ministro. La respuesta del dirigente madridista fue clara: “Si lo hacemos, lo hacemos de doble vía, que el Junior venga a Madrid y yo voy a Barranquilla”. Por ahora, no existe un acuerdo formal ni una fecha establecida para disputar los posibles compromisos. Sin embargo, la iniciativa ya fue puesta en conocimiento del alcalde de Barranquilla, Alejandro Char, con la intención de explorar las posibilidades de llevarla adelante. “No es un hecho, pero ya le conté al alcalde Char y hay que soñar. ¿Qué tal en el nuevo estadio ver a Mbappé?”, expresó Gómez, dejando entrever la ilusión de ver a figuras como Kylian Mbappé sobre el césped barranquillero. Más allá del posible enfrentamiento entre Junior y Real Madrid, el ministro resaltó las condiciones de Barranquilla para recibir espectáculos deportivos de alcance mundial. La intención también apunta a fortalecer el atractivo turístico de la ciudad, generar repercusión internacional y despertar el interés de visitantes e inversionistas. “Barranquilla está en el epicentro del mundo hoy. Todo el mundo habla de nuestra ciudad”, manifestó Gómez, destacando el momento que atraviesa la capital del Atlántico y la atención que está recibiendo por sus acontecimientos culturales y su proyección internacional. Si el proyecto avanza, Barranquilla podría vivir uno de los eventos futboleros más importantes de su historia reciente, con la visita de uno de los clubes más laureados del mundo. Aunque todo sigue siendo una iniciativa sin confirmación oficial, la respuesta de Florentino Pérez dejó abierta la puerta para que el renovado estadio de la ciudad reciba algún día a estrellas como Mbappé. Por ahora, los hinchas de Junior y los amantes del fútbol en Colombia solo pueden esperar y soñar con que este cruce entre el “Tiburón” y el Real Madrid se haga realidad.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd On Indiana: ‘The Offense Is A BB Gun Without Fernando Mendoza’
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd thinks Curt Cignetti got too much of the credit for Indiana’s national championship, and he says the Hoosiers’ recent offense is evidence of it.
articles.body: Colin Cowherd thinks Curt Cignetti got too much of the credit for Indiana’s national championship, and he says the Hoosiers’ recent offense is evidence of it. On Wednesday’s episode of "The Herd," Cowherd said the quarterback who led that title run, Fernando Mendoza, who is now the starter for the Las Vegas Raiders, deserved at least half of it. Cowherd's comments come as the defending champions prepare to host No. 18 USC on Saturday. Indiana fell five spots to No. 9 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings during its bye week. "Under Curt Cignetti, the offense is a BB gun without Fernando Mendoza," Cowherd said. "He’s a really, really good coach. But he’s not [Nick] Saban." Cowherd began by saying he works for a company with a stake in the Big Ten, and that he loves the Cignetti story. "I think the Curt Cignetti story is awesome. I think it’s been a little overplayed," Cowherd said. "I thought he got about 90% of the credit for their national championship, and I think Mendoza deserved at least half of it." He pointed to Cignetti’s 35-3 record since taking over at Indiana. But he added Indiana is different from the Alabama teams Nick Saban built. "His record is otherworldly. It’s 35-3 as he took over a bad program," Cowherd said. "He’s a really, really good coach, but he’s not Saban. Saban, both sides of the ball. Players became irrelevant at Alabama. Offense, defense, you couldn’t separate them. They were great at both. That’s not what Indiana is. Indiana, he sets a very high floor foundationally and culturally. Mendoza was the ceiling." Cowherd pointed to Indiana’s record against ranked opponents with and without Mendoza. "If you look at Indiana against ranked opponents under Curt Cignetti, when Mendoza played, they averaged 38 a game and win by three touchdowns," Cowherd said. "Without Mendoza, including this year, they’re 0-3 and they score 15 points. Mendoza against ranked teams is 6-0 and dropping 38." He also questioned Cignetti’s offensive philosophy and the 16-0 team. "Cignetti is super conservative. Nick Saban was not offensively. He’s not the recruiter of Saban," Cowherd said. "I think he’s a very, very good coach, but he got an incredible amount of the love on that 16-0 team that could have easily lost five games if Mendoza wasn’t the quarterback." Cowherd said that isn’t a knock on Cignetti, and he doesn’t think Mendoza will be Peyton Manning, but he did say he wouldn’t be surprised if USC wins Saturday. "I would not be shocked if they lost to USC. I really wouldn’t. They’re both off a bye. I wouldn’t be shocked," Cowherd said. "I think USC’s got much more firepower offensively." When asked about Indiana dropping in the rankings, Cowherd named three teams he thinks can win the national title this season. "I don’t spend a lot of time on where these are ranked," Cowherd said. "I think Georgia, Notre Dame, Miami are the only three teams that can win a national championship." FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Roll The Tape: Can Kirk Cousins Save The Vikings' Super Bowl Hopes?
articles.summary: After diving into the All-22 coaches' film from Week 9, Bucky Brooks examines three new developments to watch.
articles.body: The Minnesota Vikings have a new quarterback. The Green Bay Packers might have the most dangerous duo on offense. The Los Angeles Rams finally have their dominant duo on defense. Each week, I dive into the All-22 coaches' film before offering a few insights to watch. Here are three developments that could be long-term storylines involving some of the best teams and players in the NFL. 1.How Kirk Cousins Could Transform the Vikings' Offense Christmas came early for the Vikings, who received a huge gift in the form of Kirk Cousins via a desperate trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. The deal reunites Minnesota's old QB1 with Kevin O’Connell, as the frustrated head coach and offensive playcaller tries to revive a dormant offense that has scored only 11 offensive touchdowns this season. Although some would call a third-round pick a hefty price for a 38-year-old quarterback nearing the end of his NFL run, the Vikings’ putrid offense has desperately needed a point guard to spread the ball around to a collection of electric playmakers who have been stymied by miserable quarterback play since the start of the 2025 season. While Kyler Murray was expected to jumpstart the unit, the two-time Pro Bowler has been injured and ineffective since Week 1. And with Carson Wentz virtually unplayable as a fill-in on Monday night, the Vikings were forced to bring back their old franchise quarterback to see if he can save their title hopes with rock-solid pocket play. Despite coming off his worst performance of the season in Week 9 against the 49ers, Cousins is an upgrade over his predecessors because of his scheme knowledge and willingness to force-feed the ball to Justin Jefferson on the perimeter. The veteran enjoyed a stellar run with KOC in 2022, throwing for 4,547 yards and 29 touchdowns while leading Minnesota to a 13-4 record. Jefferson was the biggest beneficiary of Cousins' presence, earning Offensive Player of the Year honors after tallying 128 receptions, 1,809 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Cousins was producing at an even more prolific rate in 2023 through eight games (2,331 yards, 18 TDs, 5 INTs) before tearing his Achilles, which marked the end of his first stint with the Vikings. While it is unlikely Cousins can hit those numbers at his advanced age, he arrives in Minneapolis having thrown for multiple touchdowns in seven of his nine starts with the Raiders this season. As a touch-and-timing passer with great anticipation, Cousins will enable KOC to work the middle of the field with traditional drop-back and play-action concepts. Additionally, his familiarity with the offense should allow the Vikings to use the back pages of the playbook, leading to more "scheme it up" touchdowns to wideouts Jefferson and Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson on exotic play designs. With Cousins also understanding the nuances of the system and how to get the offense into the perfect call against bastardized looks, the Vikings’ overall efficiency should improve with a better pre-snap process at the line. Whether that means calling a run into a "light box" or checking into the perfect "hot" route to counter a blitz, Cousins’ experience and expertise should bode well for an offense that has struggled to move the ball, much less put points on the board. Granted, KOC and Cousins will need time to get on the same page after spending so much time apart, but the chemistry and connection between the playcaller and playmaker should lead to better play from a unit that simply requires competent quarterback play. While achieving postseason success with Cousins is a daunting challenge (he has won just one of his four career postseason starts, and those were all during his prime), the 6-2 Vikings desperately needed the veteran back to give them a chance to make a run this year. 2.Meet The Hottest Receiving Tandem In The NFL Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love has emerged as an MVP candidate in 2026, but the ascension of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden as the league’s most explosive receiving duo is currently generating just as much buzz within league circles. While the Packers’ co-WR1s have been impressive throughout the season, their Week 9 dismantling of Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots has evaluators singing their praises. In helping the Packers earn a 45-27 win, Watson and Golden became the first teammates to finish with 150-plus receiving yards and a touchdown since 2023. Moreover, they put on a 60-minute exhibition of superior route-running and playmaking that should serve as teaching tape for aspiring receivers looking to elevate their games. Watson is the classic vertical receiver on the outside, with his size, speed and length creating mismatches on the perimeter. The fifth-year pro is a blur on downfield routes, using his long strides and sneaky acceleration to blow past defenders. Measuring at 6-foot-4, 208 pounds, with a verified 4.36 40 time at the 2022 NFL Scouting Combine, Watson leads the league with 17 big-play catches (20-plus yards) while averaging 17.9 yards per catch and 97.7 receiving yards per game. Watson has developed into one of the deep-ball specialists in the business, sporting a 50% catch rate on passes covering 20-plus air yards (nine receptions on 18 targets for 354 yards) and a 39.3 yards-per-catch average on those throws in 2026, per Next Gen Stats. The 5-foot-11 Golden is nearly as productive as an explosive playmaker with 14 "big-play" snags, tied for the fourth-most in the NFL. As a high-volume receiver, the 2025 first-rounder specializes in getting open using crafty releases and top-of-the-route moves to create significant separation at the break point. He is sneaky effective as a downfield target, averaging 41.3 yards per catch on seven receptions that covered at least 20 air yards. Additionally, he is averaging 87.0 receiving yards per game. Although his catch rate is less than ideal (57.6%), Golden makes up for his inconsistencies with spectacular "catch-and-run" plays, logging 245 YAC (yards after catch) yards, which ranks 17th in the NFL. With the 6-3 Packers relying heavily on the passing game to move the ball because of their struggles on the ground, the emerging duo is showing up and showing out as arguably the best 1-2 receiving punch in football. 3.Don't Write Off The Rams And Their DPOY Duo It took until Week 9 for the football world to see the collaboration that defensive enthusiasts had been waiting for as superstar defensive linemen Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald lined up beside one another against the Washington Commanders. The future gold jacket wearers have combined for five Defensive Player of the Year awards, 13 first-team All-Pro selections, 239.5 total sacks and 328 tackles for loss between them. Even with Donald in the twilight of his career, the sight of No. 99 alongside No. 95 on the Rams’ defensive front changes everything for opponents. Garrett’s speed, explosiveness and athleticism from the edges overwhelm offensive tackles, while Donald can still wreak havoc on interior blockers with his strength, power and relentless effort. The perennial All-Pros routinely have their way with blockers, using a mix of finesse and power moves to get to the quarterback on pivotal downs. Against the Commanders, we finally got a chance to catch a glimpse of how Garrett and Donald would work together at the point of attack. The results were spectacular: The Rams held the Commanders to 5.0 yards per play while registering four sacks on the 23 snaps they were on the field together. Compared to the 8.0 yards per play and the touchdown allowed during the 19 plays they were both off the field, the Rams’ defensive resurgence, sparked by the veterans, will force the rest of the league to take notice. Garrett, who generated six pressures and three sacks on 27 pass rushes (22.2% pressure rate), looked like the reigning Defensive Player of the Year in his first action since Week 1. He looked fully back from knee surgery, whipping the Commanders’ offensive line with basketball moves he’s patented at the line of scrimmage. Whether it was the classic "Euro-step" on his strip-sack of Jayden Daniels (his first sack of the game) or the crossover move that led to his third sack, Garrett’s freakish athleticism creates problems for lumbering defenders at the line. Schematically, Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula used a hardwood concept to create favorable matchups for Garrett to tap into his hoops repertoire on the grass. On Garrett's third sack of the game, the Rams aligned in a "Double Eagle" front with the five-time All-Pro positioned over the center at five yards depth. Donald and defensive end Braden Fiske (No. 55) lined up outside the offensive guards, with outside linebackers Byron Young (No. 0) and Josaiah Stewart (No. 10) aligned on the outside shoulders of the offensive tackle. The pre-snap alignment isolated Garrett at center, with Donald and Fiske creating a bigger runway by taking outside releases to the offensive tackles after the snap. With Young and Stewart bluffing and bailing into coverage, the Rams won with a three-man rush that gave Garrett plenty of room to work over Commanders center Matt Glubin with a hesitation "dip-and-rip" move or a crossover that showcased his athleticism and basketball skills in the clutch. Although the Commanders’ game was a showcase for Garrett, Donald’s presence at the line of scrimmage is noteworthy as well. The veteran has generated multiple pressures in each of the past five games, and his pressure rate has increased despite not registering a sack yet. With the Rams’ offensive firepower potentially muted by Davante Adams and Puka Nacua on the sidelines, the defensive front’s resurgence might be enough to salvage the club's playoff hopes.

articles.title: Alyssa Thomas’ Caitlin Clark incident sparks fresh WNBA officiating controversy as Zena Keita questions referees’ biggest missed call
articles.summary: The WNBA’s handling of Alyssa Thomas’ contact with Caitlin Clark during a June game has raised fresh questions about the league’s officiating.
articles.body: The WNBA’s handling of Alyssa Thomas’ contact with Caitlin Clark during a June game has raised fresh questions about the league’s officiating. The referees did not call a foul when Thomas made contact with Clark’s throat while trying to get up from the floor. Although the league later handed Thomas a Flagrant 2 and a one-game suspension, The Athletic writer Zena Keita believes the officials should have dealt with the incident during the game itself.Zena Keita questions WNBA referees over Alyssa Thomas and Caitlin Clark incidentThe incident took place on June 24, 2026, when the Phoenix Mercury faced the Indiana Fever at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. During a fight for the ball, Thomas fell over Clark. As she tried to get back on her feet, her fist made contact with Clark’s throat. The referees did not call a foul at the time, and the play became a major talking point after the game.The WNBA reviewed the footage and announced its decision on June 25. According to the league’s official statement, Thomas had recklessly made contact with Clark’s throat area in what it described as a non-basketball act. She received a Flagrant Foul 2 penalty and a one-game suspension.However, the decision to take action after the game did not address the main concern raised by Keita. Speaking on The Athletic’s No Offseason podcast, the WNBA writer questioned why the officials had not taken action when the incident happened.“Two seasons back-to-back of high-profile moments…this season involving Alyssa Thomas and Caitlin Clark, in which Alyssa Thomas was not ejected during the game and removed for a Flagrant 2 for unintentionally putting her full weight on Caitlin Clark and in her neck area to get up off the floor in a game. It should have been called,” Keita said.She also explained why the location of the contact mattered, regardless of whether Thomas meant to hurt Clark.“Whether you want to argue about the intention or not, the fact is that should not have happened, and it should have been um adjudicated in that moment.”Napheesa Collier’s WNBA officiating criticism adds to growing concernsKeita’s comments also bring back the criticism Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier made during her 2025 season-ending interview. After the Lynx were eliminated by the Mercury in the semifinals, Collier spoke openly about the league’s handling of officiating and player safety. She was particularly unhappy with the lack of action when players faced dangerous contact on the court.“Since I’ve been in the league, you’ve heard the constant concerns about officiating, and it has now reached levels of inconsistency that plague our sport and undermine the integrity in which it operates,” Collier said.She also questioned whether the league was doing enough to protect its players, adding that poor officiating could affect the quality of the game. Her comments attracted attention because they came from a player who had spent years competing at the highest level of the WNBA.The concerns are not limited to Collier and Keita. Caitlin Clark has also spoken about missed calls during games, while coaches have raised questions about how consistently referees handle physical plays. The issue has become particularly noticeable during games involving Clark, where fans have often questioned whether officials are giving her enough protection.The WNBA has now taken a step towards improving its review process. In an official announcement on July 25, 2026, the league confirmed that it would introduce centralized Replay Center operations from the beginning of the 2027 season.The system will use the NBA’s Replay Center in Secaucus, New Jersey, giving officials access to different camera angles and additional support when reviewing plays. All WNBA arenas will be connected to the facility, allowing replay officials to help referees make more accurate decisions on situations that qualify for review.This change is part of the league’s investment in officiating and competitive fairness. However, as Keita’s comments suggest, getting the right decision during a game remains just as important as correcting it afterwards.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: College Basketball Catchup: Michigan Rebounds, Vandy Got Better, UCLA Is Hot
articles.summary: Michigan bounces back, Mia Woolfolk shows why Vanderbilt wanted her, Ethan Roberts makes Notre Dame history and more from Wednesday's college basketball action.
articles.body: Michigan bounced back after a loss to UConn. A second-year forward looks like she's taking the leap for Mississippi State. UCLA is hot, hot, hot to start the season. Here's what you need to know from yesterday's slate of college basketball. Coach's Corner: Boynton On Costello Michigan is in a tough position. At least, relative to a year ago, when the Wolverines were one of the top teams for almost the entire season, and then ended up being national champions. Now, though, Michigan has a new coach — Mike Boynton — and some new players, too, and lost to UConn already. On Wednesday, Michigan faced off against Marquette at home, and came away with an 84-70 victory. Tennessee transfer J.P. Estrella played a significant role, with the senior forward scoring 18 with eight rebounds and two assists in his 31 minutes, but right up there with Estrella was freshman Quinn Costello. In 25 minutes off the bench, the forward scored 15 points, all on threes: he was 5-for-6 from beyond the arc, and didn’t shoot once from inside it. Mike Boynton had nothing but positive things to say about Costello postgame. "I’ve coached some really good shooters, I’ve never coached a 6’10" guy who can shoot like he can." Boyton explained that Costello is a "high achiever" who works hard on the non-shooting aspects of his game to help the team win, but on Wednesday it was absolutely his shot that helped Michigan the most. Top Performance: Favour Nwaedozi Mississippi State’s Favour Nwaedozi is no stranger to rebounding. As a junior last year, the 6-foot-3 forward — who had arrived for her first NCAA season after spending two years playing for Mukogawa Women’s University in Japan — pulled down exactly 10 boards per game, and did so while averaging 12.2 points per, as well. That’s averaging a double-double right there. On Wednesday against Troy, Nwaedozi was right back at it, only better. She had eight rebounds just about halfway into the first quarter, and would finish the night with 19 boards and 22 points. Nwaedozi had an assist and two steals just for good measure, and shot 10-for-14 while scoring another two from the line for the top showing of the day. She currently leads all players in the SEC with 14.7 rebounds per game as well as total boards, with 44, and what’s most wild about that is she’s playing about 22 minutes per game. Her per 40 minute numbers are cartoonish: Nwaedozi is averaging 25.9 rebounds per game there. Just three games, yes, but in her second season in the SEC, a better performance than an already great one wouldn’t be a surprise. Men's Scoring Leader: Ethan Roberts Ethan Roberts joined Notre Dame history last night, sinking 10 threes in 13 attempts — he’s one of just three Fighting Irish, along with Kyle McAlarney and Matt Farrell, to make 10 threes in a single game. Roberts didn’t just score from deep, even if that was mostly where his points came from. He added another six from inside the arc to lead all scorers, men and women, on Wednesday. Notre Dame didn’t need quite that level of performance out of Roberts — the Irish defeated South Carolina State, 99-59 — but they got it all the same. Roberts is the first D-I men’s hooper this year to hit double-digit threes, but not the first D-I player to accomplish the feat in 2026: Chloe Donnell dropped 14 against Ecclesia for Northwestern State on Nov. 2. Roberts is, however, the first of the year to manage it against a Division I opponent instead of a team from a lower division. Women's Scoring Leader: Nadia Moore Unlike with Notre Dame and Roberts, the women’s scoring leader on Wednesday absolutely needed to go that hard in order for her team to win. Nadia Moore, a junior guard from Duquesne who has only this year become a regular starter, dropped a career-best 33 against Marist in a game the Dukes would win by a mere five points. Moore started hot, and finished scorching: she scored 15 of Duquesne’s 22 points in the fourth quarter, in a game the Dukes would win 72-67. She helped out with more than just pure scoring, too, as Moore dished out four assists, grabbed a steal and secured five rebounds, and shot accurately at 69% overall and 4-for-7 on treys. She had never scored even 20 points in a game before, with her previous career-best sitting at 18. Coming into Wednesday, Moore had just three games on her résumé in which she scored more points than she did in the fourth quarter of this one alone. Marist certainly wasn’t ready for that shift. One Name To Know: Mia Woolfolk Mia Woolfolk had two pretty good seasons for Georgia before transferring to Vanderbilt for the 2026-2027 season. With the Commodores, she’s going to have more help than she did on the Bulldogs, and Woolfolk is also going to make Vandy better than it was, too. Against Western Kentucky last night, Woolfolk was unstoppable in the paint. She took 14 shots and missed just two, sank three of four from the charity stripe, and grabbed three boards and a steal while she was busy in the paint, too. Sophomore guard Aubrey Galvan — see above clip — is already enjoying having Woolfolk hanging around in the paint as another scoring option to pass to, and her constant threat there is going to create opportunities for All-American Mikayla Blakes to take better shots this season, too: a terrifying proposition, considering Blakes led Division I in scoring last season with 27 points per game. Before You Go: UCLA's Hot Start No. 9 UCLA is off to a terrific start this year. The Bruins have averaged 101.3 points per game across their first three contests, dropping 84, 114 and 106 points so far. That 84 was no joke, either, because it came against then-No. 5 Arizona in the Bruins’ first dub of the season. UCLA’s women’s team is the defending national champion; the men’s team hasn’t won since the 1994-1995 season, however, when the Bruins won their still-men’s-record 11th title. Mick Cronin’s squad has quite a bit of season left to get through, but that win against Arizona and the subsequent beatdown against opponents the Bruins should be winning is at least making this team seem like one that has something to show the rest of the league this year. articles.title: La nueva Colombia ya está aquí: el once titular que usaría Néstor Lorenzo para el partido contra Chile
articles.standfirst: Posible formación titular de la Selección Colombia vs. Chile: el XI que prepara Néstor Lorenzo en Cali
articles.summary: Posible formación titular de la Selección Colombia vs. Chile: el XI que prepara Néstor Lorenzo en Cali
articles.body: La Selección Colombia se encuentra ultimando detalles en la sede deportiva de Cascajal (América de Cali) con la mira puesta en su regreso al estadio Olímpico Pascual Guerrero. El combinado nacional cerrará su calendario de partidos del año 2026 enfrentando a la selección de Chile en un doble amistoso correspondiente a la última Fecha FIFA de la temporada. El primer pulso se disputará este viernes 13 de noviembre a partir de las 7:00 p. m. en territorio vallecaucano, mientras que el segundo asalto tendrá lugar en Santiago el próximo martes 17. Para este reto, el director técnico Néstor Lorenzo ha preparado una convocatoria cargada de renovación, sorpresas y ajustes obligados debido a lesiones de peso, apostando por una mezcla entre la experiencia internacional de la columna vertebral y el talento emergente que pide pista en el rentado local e internacional. El proceso del estratega argentino afronta esta doble fecha con ausencias significativas que han condicionado la planificación del once inicial. Futbolistas habituales y referentes del proceso como Luis Díaz, Richard Ríos, Juan Camilo 'Cucho' Hernández y Kevin Viveros no pudieron ser tenidos en cuenta debido a sus respectivos procesos de recuperación física. Asimismo, la lista de convocados dejó fuera a ocho nombres que venían sumando minutos en ciclos anteriores —entre ellos Álvaro Montero, Kevin Mier, Kevin Castaño y Carlos Andrés Gómez—, abriendo la puerta a nuevas caras como el lateral Juan David Arizala (Udinese) y los delanteros Daniel Mosquera (Hellas Verona) y Camilo Mena (Korona Kielce). Sin embargo, el gran dilema táctico de Lorenzo pasa por configurar un equipo equilibrado que mantenga la intensidad competitiva y responda ante la expectativa de la afición caleña. De acuerdo con los últimos ensayos tácticos realizados en suelo vallecaucano, Néstor Lorenzo apostaría por un esquema estructurado bajo un 4-2-3-1, donde la gran novedad pasa por la inclusión en el mediocampo de Nelson Deossa. El volante, de gran momento en el fútbol internacional con el Real Betis, se perfila para tomar las riendas de la zona medular junto a la experiencia y solidez de Jefferson Lerma (Crystal Palace), ganándole la pulseada a alternativas como Gustavo Puerta. La alineación probable que saltaría al gramado del Pascual Guerrero estaría conformada de la siguiente manera: Arquero: Camilo Vargas (Atlas) Defensas: Daniel Muñoz, Dávinson Sánchez, Jhon Lucumí y Samuel Velásquez. Volantes de primera línea: Jefferson Lerma y Nelson Deossa. Volantes ofensivos: Jhon Arias, Juan Manuel Rengifo y Camilo Durán. Delantero centro: Luis Javier Suárez. En el arco, aunque la veteranía de Camilo Vargas parece asegurar su lugar de arranque, no se descarta que el cuerpo técnico le dé minutos en alguno de los dos amistosos a Devis Vásquez (AS Roma) o Aldair Quintana para evaluar alternativas bajo los tres palos de cara al futuro. La capital del Valle del Cauca ha vivido una fiesta desde la llegada de las delegaciones. La boletería habilitada a través de plataformas oficiales ha tenido una respuesta masiva por parte de los hinchas, restando únicamente localidades en sectores específicos como la tribuna occidental del escenario deportivo. Para Néstor Lorenzo, estos noventa minutos en Cali no son solo un examen de preparación, sino la oportunidad perfecta para consolidar sociedades futbolísticas y evaluar el rendimiento de piezas jóvenes que buscan asentarse definitivamente en el radar de la Selección Colombia de cara a los desafíos oficiales venideros.

articles.summary: La Selección Colombia Sub-17 enciende la ilusión mundialista con una joya europea y talento puro del FPC
articles.body: La ilusión de todo un país vuelve a ponerse en marcha en las divisiones menores del balompié nacional. La Selección Colombia Masculina Sub-17 oficializó su lista definitiva de 21 jugadores convocados por el director técnico Fredy Hurtado, con la mira puesta en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA Catar 2026, que se disputará del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre. Tras firmar una campaña memorable que la consagró campeona del Sudamericano de la categoría —dejando exhibiciones de jerarquía como el contundente 4-0 sobre Argentina en la gran final y un brillante paso ante Brasil—, la Tricolor pule sus armas para trascender en territorio asiático. El estratega Fredy Hurtado ha estructurado una nómina equilibrada que reconoce el esfuerzo de los procesos de formación en el Fútbol Profesional Colombiano, combinándolo con talento de exportación. Los clubes locales aportan el grueso de la plantilla: Atlético Nacional encabeza la lista con cinco futbolistas, seguido muy de cerca por Independiente Medellín con cuatro aportes fundamentales. A ellos se suman promesas de instituciones tradicionales como el Deportivo Cali, Envigado F.C., Barranquilla F.C., Fortaleza y C.D. Estudiantil. No obstante, uno de los grandes atractivos mediáticos y deportivos de esta convocatoria es la inclusión de Gorka Abascal, mediocampista que milita en las divisiones inferiores del Real Madrid C.F. de España. Nacido en Bilbao y vinculado a la selección gracias a su ascendencia materna (tras pasar por las canteras del Deusto, Danok Bat y Athletic Club), Abascal se perfila como una de las piezas diferentes en la zona medular del combinado patrio. Entre los 21 elegidos para buscar la gloria orbital sobresalen nombres propios que ya saben lo que es brillar bajo presión: José Escorcia (Atlético Nacional): Uno de los motores creativos y ofensivos del equipo. Fue determinante en el Sudamericano al reportarse con cuatro anotaciones y dos asistencias, consolidándose como el faro en la mitad de la cancha. Samuel Martínez (Atlético Nacional / Envigado): Su liderazgo en la zona medular y lectura táctica le han valido para portar el rótulo de estandarte en la columna vertebral diseñada por el cuerpo técnico. Gorka Abascal (Real Madrid): Aporta la visión europea, intensidad en la recuperación y criterio en la distribución del balón, siendo el único representante de la plantilla que actúa en el fútbol del viejo continente. Aporte ofensivo: Hombres como Adrián Mosquera (Independiente Medellín) y Matías Caicedo (Atlético Huila / Yumbo) cargarán con la responsabilidad de traducir el volumen de juego en anotaciones determinantes para superar la fase de grupos. Colombia quedó sembrada en el Grupo L del certamen orbital, un cuadrangular exigente donde compartirá zona con selecciones de recorrido internacional: Japón Honduras Serbia Todos los encuentros de esta primera fase se disputarán en el imponente complejo deportivo Aspire Zone, en Catar. El calendario estipulado para la fase de grupos (con horarios ajustados a la hora de Colombia) es el siguiente: Sábado, 21 de noviembre: Japón vs. Colombia | 4:30 a. m. / 7:30 a. m.* Martes, 24 de noviembre: Honduras vs. Colombia | 10:30 a. m. Viernes, 27 de noviembre: Colombia vs. Serbia | 8:00 a. m. La delegación nacional emprenderá su viaje rumbo a Doha con la firme convicción de superar las mejores actuaciones históricas de Colombia en la categoría Sub-17, cuando se alcanzó el cuarto puesto en las ediciones de 2003 y 2009. Con una mezcla equilibrada de disciplina táctica, talento desequilibrante en el frente de ataque y el respaldo de una generación que dominó el continente, la Tricolor alista sus maletas para regalarle una nueva alegría al país en tierras cataríes.

articles.title: Miguel García de Blas, experto en tecnología, revela que Apple va a “acabar” con este botón en sus teléfonos: “Lo odio”
articles.standfirst: El colaborador ha explicado todos los detalles en redes sociales
articles.summary: El colaborador ha explicado todos los detalles en redes sociales
articles.body: Apple es la empresa tecnológica más importante del mundo, por lo que cualquier novedad en relación a sus dispositivos se convierte en noticia. En este sentido, Miguel García de Blas, experto en tecnología, ha revelado que la marca fundada por Steve Wozniak y Steve Jobs pretende “acabar” con uno de los botones más icónicos de sus teléfonos: el de acción. “Apple va a eliminar uno de los botones que más odio de los iPhone, sinceramente. O sea, es verdad que no es el que más ultraodio, pero es que los odio casi todos. La noticia dice que está pensando en eliminar el botón de acción de los iPhone. No el botón de cámara, que es mi archienemigo. No, no, el botón de acción”, comienza diciendo el especialista a través de las redes sociales de Topes de Gama, medio especializado en tecnología en el que colabora habitualmente. El experto apunta que los rumores dicen que dicho botón podría ya no aparecer en los iPhone que llegarán en la segunda mitad del año que viene, aunque esto no está confirmado. “Entonces, en vez de eliminar el botón de cámara, que era el que realmente aporta poco, sinceramente, eliminan el botón de acción, que por lo menos le podías meter ahí tus atajos, tus cositas y más o menos te lo dejabas apañado”, afirma. Tras ello, ha explicado dónde van a ir incorporadas las funciones del botón de acción: “Dicen que básicamente este botón de acción se elimina físicamente, pero las funciones de este botón de acción pasan al botón de cámara. Es decir, un solo toque al botón de cámara abriría la cámara, una pulsación prolongada del botón de cámara abriría la acción que tengas configurada en ese botón de acción que teníamos hasta ahora”. Finalmente, Miguel García de Blas señala que es “una decisión cuanto menos polémica” y que duda de “si esto llegará para los iPhone 18 básicos o se quedará para ese iPhone del 20 aniversario”. Lo que está claro es que Apple no da puntada sin hilo”, sentencia el especialista en la materia.

articles.standfirst: La pareja 5 del torneo cayó a manos de Javi Garrido y Juani de Pascual en tres sets
articles.summary: La pareja 5 cayó a manos de Garrido y De Pascual en tres sets
articles.body: El Dubai P1 de Premier Padel ya conoce a sus cuartofinalistas tras una jornada intensa en la que, como ya sucediese en los días anteriores, varias parejas importantes se quedaron por el camino. La eliminación más destacada ha sido la de Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas, cabezas de serie número 5, que no pudieron superar a Juani de Pascual y a Javi Garrido en una batalla de tres sets que acabó decidiéndose en el tiebreak (7-6, 3-6 y 7-6) y que, de momento, complica el Tour Finals a Coki. Sus rivales serán Franco Stupaczuk y Jon Sanz, que se deshicieron de Maxi Sánchez Blasco y Sanyo Gutiérrez (6-3 y 6-4) en el último duelo del día en la prueba emiratí. Por el mismo lado del cuadro, la pareja ganadora se medirá a la que se lleve el duelo entre Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso ante Jairo Bautista y Lucas Bergamini. Por el otro lado, los favoritos a llevarse esta prueba, teniendo en cuenta que las dos primeras parejas no están, tampoco se dejaron sorprender. Leo Augsburger y Juan Lebrón tumbaron fácil a Víctor Ruiz y Facundo López (6-2 y 6-4) y se encontrarán en cuartos con Maxi Arce y Juan Tello, que se llevaron otra de las batallas del día ante Edu Alonso y Aimar Goñi (3-6, 6-3 y 6-2). El cruce será con el que se lleve el duelo entre dos parejas que sueñan en grande. Flavio Abbate y Franco dal Bianco, que aspiran a meterse en semis por primera vez en Premier Padel, se las verán con Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo, sobre el papel favoritos y que ya han pisado esta ronda tres veces este año. Jimena Velasco y Raquel Eugenio protagonizaron la gran sorpresa en el femenino eliminando a Marta Ortega y Sofía Araujo, pareja 5, en tres sets (4-6, 6-4 y 6-3). Se medirán en cuartos a Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, que siguen inmersas en la pelea por el 1 y que no pueden fallar. Las números 1, Gemma Triay y Delfina Brea, tendrán enfrente mañana un hueso duro de roer: Claudia Jensen y Tamara Icardo. Por su parte, Bea y Paula, que también apuran sus opciones de acabar en lo más alto del ránking, se medirán a Marina Guinart y Alejandra Alonso.

articles.title: Senegal’s wrestlers turn tradition into gold at Dakar Youth Olympics
articles.summary: Senegal’s young wrestlers thrive as they adapt skills from their traditional sport to beach wrestling at Youth Olympics.
articles.body:
Sixteen-year-old Elisabeth Diatta is from the southern Senegalese region of Casamance. Football was her sport, not wrestling.

Yet, On Saturday, there she was on the sand at Saly beach, representing Senegal in beach wrestling at Dakar’s Youth Olympics , almost instinctively seizing her opponent and throwing her down. Then came the whistle, the referee’s look, the confirmation, the disbelief. She celebrated like Cristiano Ronaldo; the leap, the turn, the “Siu!”

At 16, she had beaten Japan’s Reisa Kojima 5-1 in the 55kg final to win Senegal’s first Youth Olympic gold.

A teenage girl had delivered a medal in a sport so often described as belonging to men.

The crowd roared. Diatta danced, defiant, before wrapping herself in green, yellow and red. Beneath the Senegalese flag’s green star, a new star was born.

Her path here began when her older sister Jeannine was injured and could not enter a wrestling tournament at a sport camp. Diatta took her place. She won her first bout. The footballer kept wrestling.

“They said wrestling would make me less feminine,” explains Diatta – the “they” she is referring to are the adults around here. Out of teenage defiance, she persisted in the sport.

Watching proudly was coach Isabelle Sambou, twice an Olympian herself. She had wanted this gold for Senegal long before her young wrestlers were old enough to compete.

“I wanted to win gold for Senegal when I was an athlete,” she said. “Today, I have my reward.”

She would soon have another reason to celebrate as another Senegalese teenage hopeful, 16-year-old Maguette Diop, stepped into the wrestling circle later on Saturday. Diop had been preparing for this moment long before the games, being held from October 31 to November 13 in the Senegalese capital Dakar and nearby towns of Saly and Diamniadio.

Three months in an intense training camp had helped Senegal’s young wrestlers adapt to beach wrestling, where the rules differed from those of their traditional sport.

In traditional Senegalese wrestling, a wrestler wins by bringing their opponent to the ground, typically onto their back, buttocks or knees, or by forcing them onto all fours. Unlike beach wrestling, there is no points system. One decisive fall can end the contest.

In beach wrestling, forcing an opponent outside the circle earns one point, as does a takedown. A throw onto the back earns three and ends the contest. Bouts last up to three minutes; the first to at least three points wins.

Diop had spent months preparing for this moment. On August 27, he had lost to Iran’s Reza Jalilian in the semifinals of the under-17 world championships in Baku. Barely two months later, on home ground, he was not about to let that happen again.

He reached the boys’ 80kg final feeling confident despite facing Azerbaijan’s Nihad Suleymanli, a two-time under-17 world champion. Suleymani wrestled with skill, ignoring the crowd cheering for Diop.

For a moment, the gold appeared to be slipping away. The referee awarded Suleymanli three points. Diop’s coaches urged a challenge. The replay reversed the decision: Those points belonged to Diop. He had won 4-0.

More dancing. More flags. Another Senegalese teenager with gold.

Here, wrestling runs deep. Long before the Olympic flame reached this Atlantic coastline, generations had gathered around circles of sand.

Laamb, Senegal’s traditional wrestling, carries the pride of villages and neighbourhoods. It is more than a contest of strength. Wrestlers seek spiritual protection through prayers, rituals and amulets believed to ward off evil spirits. All to the rhythm of sabar drums, traditional Senegalese percussion whose beats accompany the ceremonial dances, summoning courage and stirring the crowd.

In Casamance, where Diatta comes from, women have long wrestled too, even as men dominate the professional arenas.

“I hope this experience will give girls courage and determination,” said Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta, who added a third Senegalese gold in the 45kg category the following day.

By Thursday, Senegal stood sixth in the medal table – three of their five golds won wrestling on the sand.

For Africa, hosting its first Olympic sporting event, these victories offered something the rankings could not measure: young people seeing themselves in the athletes wearing gold, a familiar sport carrying them onto a world stage.

And for the girls watching Senegal’s female wrestlers, perhaps something closer still. A place inside the circle.

articles.title: El fetiche del neopreno que dispara los ingresos de una surfista
articles.standfirst: Erika White asegura haber pasado de limpiar baños para sobrevivir a ingresar hasta 50.000 libras mensuales en OnlyFans. El secreto de parte de su éxito es tan inesperado como polémico: algunos seguidores pagan por verla completamente cubierta con su traje de surf.
articles.summary: Erika White asegura haber pasado de limpiar baños para sobrevivir a ingresar hasta 50.000 libras mensuales en OnlyFans. El secreto de parte de su éxito es tan inesperado como polémico: algunos seguidores pagan por verla completamente cubierta con su traje de surf.
articles.body: Lo que antes no podía permitirse comprar ahora le ayuda a ganar miles de libras. La surfista británica Erika White, afincada cerca de Byron Bay (Australia), ha revelado uno de los aspectos más insólitos de su actividad en OnlyFans: algunos suscriptores pagan específicamente por verla vestida con un traje de neopreno. Una afición que, según cuenta, le ha permitido convertir una prenda imprescindible para surfear en una fuente de ingresos que jamás habría imaginado. La historia de White tiene un pasado muy diferente al de su actual vida en Australia. Antes de crear contenido para adultos, intentaba abrirse camino en el surf mediante pequeñas colaboraciones comerciales, patrocinios de material y publicaciones sobre su estilo de vida. Sin embargo, esos ingresos no eran suficientes. La propia surfista reconoce que llegó a limpiar baños y depender de ayudas públicas para mantenerse económicamente. Su situación cambió con OnlyFans. Según las cifras que ella misma ha comunicado a SURFER, sus ingresos mensuales pasaron de unas 5.000 a 50.000 libras en ocho meses. Un crecimiento extraordinario que, conviene precisar, no ha sido verificado de manera independiente. Lo más sorprendente de su relato es que algunos seguidores no quieren verla quitarse el traje, sino precisamente lo contrario. White explica que existe un grupo de suscriptores especialmente interesado en los trajes de neopreno ajustados, incluidos los modelos de invierno que cubren prácticamente todo el cuerpo. La surfista asegura que ha llegado a cobrar simplemente por aparecer vestida con ese equipamiento, aunque ella misma no lo considera necesariamente sexual. Para determinados seguidores, en cambio, el atractivo está precisamente en el material y en cómo se ajusta al cuerpo. El caso de White refleja una transformación cada vez más visible en los deportes de acción. Mientras algunos surfistas profesionales, como Billy Kemper o Jacob «Zeke» Szekely, utilizan OnlyFans para compartir entrenamientos y contenidos exclusivos, otros creadores han encontrado fórmulas de monetización completamente diferentes. La diferencia es importante: tener presencia en OnlyFans no implica necesariamente publicar contenido para adultos, del mismo modo que el éxito económico de White no puede extrapolarse al conjunto de los surfistas que utilizan la plataforma. Su historia plantea una cuestión incómoda para la industria: ¿cómo es posible que una creadora vinculada al surf encuentre una rentabilidad tan elevada fuera de los patrocinios tradicionales? En el caso de Erika White, la respuesta es tan peculiar como reveladora. El neopreno que antes representaba un gasto difícil de asumir se ha convertido en parte de su negocio, permitiéndole financiar los viajes y la vida alrededor del surf que siempre había querido.

articles.title: New NHL Rumors Detail Matvei Michkov's Talks With Flyers Teammates Before Video of Heated Exchange
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers held a meeting to try and build camaraderie between players shortly before forward Matvei Michkov and veteran defenseman Nick Seeler clashed in what appeared to be a heated mid-game exchange Monday evening, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Thursday.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers held a meeting to try and build camaraderie between players shortly before forward Matvei Michkov and veteran defenseman Nick Seeler clashed in what appeared to be a heated mid-game exchange Monday evening, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Thursday.

ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported the day after that incident Michkov "would likely want a new start elsewhere," although the Flyers have since said Michkov hasn't formally requested a trade.

"Over the last 24 hours, I heard some crazy stories about the relationship between Michkov and his teammates," Friedman said around the 9:30 mark of Thursday's 32 Thoughts: The Podcast .

Friedman continued, "One of the reasons everybody is disappointed by what happened in the last 24 to 48 hours is that there was a recent get-together, meal, whatever, between some of the players including Michkov to work on this. Like, a legit attempt. 'Let's hold hands, kumbaya, work together, be a team.'

"And then there was this explosion on the bench... I think they did something recently to all pull together, and then this happened."

ESPN's Emily Kaplan previously reported that "sources said there has been turmoil behind the scenes between Michkov and the Flyers."

The clash between Michkov and Seeler happened in the second period of a 3-1 Flyers victory in Vancouver. Inside the Coaches' Room's Steve Peters pointed out Seeler had earlier in the game tapped his stick for a pass on a play during which Michkov took a shot.

Seeler, who is in his sixth season with the Flyers, has yet to score this season.

Michkov is currently leading the Flyers with 10 goals in 21 games, but he has seen his ice time fluctuate under head coach Rick Tocchet to the point he was made a healthy scratch during last spring's playoff run.

He is also a pending restricted free agent, which could make him a trade target if he doesn't plan to re-sign in Philadelphia this offseason. General manager Danny Briere still told Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli after Weekes' report the Flyers have "never discussed" a potential trade for Michkov.

The Flyers' recent rebuild took a hit when Cutter Gauthier, the No. 5 pick of the 2022 draft, reportedly indicated he didn't want to play in Philadelphia before he was traded in 2024 the Anaheim Ducks.

Philadelphia could hope to avoid parting ways with another recent high draft selection by continuing work to improve the relationship between former No. 7 pick Michkov and his teammates.

articles.title: Italy fight back to beat France 3-1 and move top of Nations League group
articles.summary: Michael Olise gives France the lead, but double from Pio Esposito and one from Davide Frattesi secure win for Italy.
articles.body:
Francesco Pio Esposito struck twice to inflict a first defeat on Zinedine Zidane as France’s head coach, while Italy stormed back to win 3-1 at San Siro and top their Nations League group.

Michael Olise profited from a Gianluigi Donnarumma error to put the visitors in front after 10 minutes on Thursday, but Italy hit back through Esposito and Davide Frattesi either side of half-time.

Inter Milan striker Esposito’s second came from the penalty spot after his brother Sebastiano had earlier fired a spot kick wide, while France were twice denied by the woodwork in an entertaining encounter.

The result sent Italy top of Group A1 on 10 points, level with France but above them on head-to-head record, while Belgium are third on nine points after inflicting a fifth straight defeat on rock-bottom Turkiye.

France were without star attackers Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele through injury, but it did not show as they made an electric start in pouring rain in Milan.

Desire Doue hit the side netting and first-time captain Adrien Rabiot tested Donnarumma before Lucas Da Cunha’s rasping half-volley flew narrowly wide.

But the opener was gifted to France when Donnarumma passed the ball straight to Olise, who skipped past a defender before firing home his fifth goal in five Nations League games – a record only bettered by England captain Harry Kane’s seven.

The hosts struck back in the 26th minute with their first chance of the game when Nicolo Cambiaghi drove to the byline and cut back a cross, which Esposito converted with a deft touch.

The goal brought San Siro to life as the older Esposito sibling, Sebastiano, threatened a quickfire comeback two minutes later, forcing a sharp save from Mike Maignan.

Bradley Barcola came closest to a third goal before the break with a curling shot from the edge of the box that struck the foot of the far post.

The end-to-end nature of the game continued in the second half as Rayan Cherki’s rasping strike was tipped onto the post by Donnarumma before Italy charged up the other end and forced Maignan into a point-blank save from Cambiaghi.

Italy had a glorious chance to go in front when Cambiaghi was tripped by Malo Gusto to earn a penalty, but Sebastiano Esposito failed to join his brother on the scoresheet as he hammered his spot kick wide on the hour mark.

The Azzurri did not dwell on the disappointment for long, taking the lead just three minutes later when Frattesi drilled in a shot from a Federico Dimarco cross moments after the Inter Milan wing-back was brought off the bench.

Fellow substitute Antonio Vergara earned the home side another penalty when he was tripped by Dayot Upamecano, and this time Francesco Pio Esposito stepped up to drill a shot into the bottom corner.

The result continued a strong start to Roberto Mancini’s second spell as Italy coach as his side stretched their unbeaten run to four matches and notched their first home win over France since 1962.

Belgium host Italy and Turkiye travel to France in the final round of group games on Sunday.

Elsewhere, captain Harry Kane celebrated his record 126th cap for England with a match-winner from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday to qualify for the Nations League last eight.

The 33-year-old followed a script that seemed destined to happen when he stepped up in the 64th minute to put England ahead in front of an 80,400-strong crowd after the hosts had conceded a sloppy equaliser five minutes earlier.

It was the Bayern Munich forward’s 92nd England goal, and there was never any doubt from the moment he placed the ball and sent it straight down the middle as goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic dived to his left.

Kane had started a night of celebration as the centre of attention, handed a commemorative token by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, the previous record holder since 1989, when he surpassed Bobby Moore’s 108 caps.

articles.title: Celtics’ Paul George Gets Bold All-Star Prediction From 17-Year NBA Veteran
articles.summary: When the Boston Celtics acquired Paul George as part of the Jaylen Brown trade, the fanbase was understandably upset. George was coming off two straight seas...
articles.body:
When the Boston Celtics acquired Paul George as part of the Jaylen Brown trade, the fanbase was understandably upset. George was coming off two straight seasons of injury issues with the Philadelphia 76ers.

However, the 36-year-old forward looks like a totally different player to begin the season in Boston. George has produced two 30-point games in his first 10 outings and has been highly impactful on both sides of the floor.

When speaking with Heavy on Sports, via US sportsbooks, 17-year NBA veteran Eddie Johnson shared his belief that George could earn his 10th All-Star appearance, should he stay healthy for the Celtics.

" If the season ended today, he'd be an All-Star," Johnson said. "This is no surprise with Paul George. I've known Paul since he was, like, 17, 18 years old. He's a tremendous basketball player. His issue has been injuries over the years, and that's kinda set him back. But his skill set on the basketball court is undeniable."

"He is an excellent player, and he's having a fantastic season. In my opinion, when they did the Jaylen Brown deal, it was that if Paul George can stay healthy, then Boston would probably have a good season. My big question with him was can he stay healthy, right? Can Tatum stay healthy? But we saw last night (against the Philadelphia 76ers) how good Paul George is, and he was the best player on the floor."

George, 36, has certainly enjoyed a hot start to his time in Boston. However, the next hurdle will be sustaining that production throughout the season.

George Was Celtics Best Player vs. Sixers

George played a key role in Boston's 123-101 win over the 76ers on Tuesday, November 10. He scored a total of 36 points, with 14 of them coming in the fourth quarter to help the Celtics close out the game.

When speaking with the media following Philadelphia's loss, Joel Embiid heaped praise on his former teammate.

"You can kind of say he's been the best player, to a certain level," Embiid told reporters.

Embiid wasn't lying when it comes to the production against Philadelphia. However, after months of discussions surrounding Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown, the former MVP may have been trying to create some division within the Celtics locker room.

Jayson Tatum Earned Praise Against Raptors

Following his game-winning exploits against the 76ers, George was rested for Boston's November 11 matchup against the Toronto Raptors . He was listed on the injury report as dealing with an illness.

In George's absence, Tatum stepped up to the plate and helped will his team to a win, earning praise from head coach Joe Mazzulla in the process.

"We didn't win the game in the fourth quarter. We won the game in the middle of the second quarter when we cut it to seven," Mazzulla said, praising the energy Tatum provided for his team. "It's a 22-point game. It could go either way. You can kind of mail it in and just say, 'Second night of a back-to-back, blah, blah, blah.'"

The Celtics will now have a few days off before getting back onto the court. Their next game is scheduled for Sunday, November 15, against the 7-4 Dallas Mavericks .

The Los Angeles Rams will need their supporting cast to step up with Puka Nacua sidelined. While Matthew Stafford has developed a strong connection with Nacua and Davante Adams, the quarterback will need to rely on his other receiving options to keep the offense productive.

Fortunately, offensive coordinator Nathan Scheelhaase believes those players are more prepared for the opportunity than their lack of involvement might suggest.

When asked how he can help Stafford develop trust in his other receivers, Scheelhaase explained that chemistry isn't something that develops overnight. The players have spent an entire season building relationships through practice repetitions and preparation.

"Trust doesn't just show up on a Sunday. It doesn't just show up on a Thursday practice either. There's been a lot of reps over the course of a year that those guys have built up trust," Scheelhaase said.

The Rams have understandably prioritized getting the football to their two biggest receiving threats when both are available. However, that doesn't mean the other players on the roster lack the ability to contribute.

Scheelhaase emphasized that Los Angeles has other receivers capable of executing when their numbers are called.

"Most of the time in this league, circumstances are what create opportunity," Scheelhaase added.

Nacua's absence creates exactly that opportunity. Stafford will have to spread the football around more, giving the Rams' other receiving options a chance to establish themselves in a larger role. Stafford has the experience and ability to make everyone around him better. Now, the Rams need their supporting cast to reward that confidence and prove they can deliver when called upon.

articles.title: Rutgers Football vs Nebraska 2026 Preview
articles.summary: The Knights gear up to face Nebraska without several key offensive pieces.
articles.body:
After falling to Wisconsin 31-10 in Madison, Rutgers football will return home to play Nebraska this weekend as a part of their military appreciation game. This game comes at the end of a long week for Scarlet Knights football, as it was announced earlier in the week that head coach Greg Schiano will be back for another year and that star wide receiver KJ Duff will be out for the season due to surgery on a high ankle injury.

Rutgers will be coming into this game on a three-game losing streak, falling to Northwestern and Wisconsin in blowout fashion and being defeated by a struggling Michigan team. Similar to the Knights, the Cornhuskers are on a long losing streak of their own, falling to Indiana, Oregon, Washington and Illinois in consecutive weeks. However, unlike Rutgers, three of these losses came by a touchdown or less.

The Cornhuskers' starting quarterback, Anthony Colandrea, has thrown for 2,100 yards and 16 touchdowns so far this season. However, after starting the year off hot, his play has taken a serious step down in this losing streak for the Huskers, as over the last four games he has thrown three touchdowns and five interceptions. Colandrea is also a good runner, rushing for an average of 4.5 yards per carry as well as four total touchdowns this season.

His best receiving option so far this season has been Kwazi Gilmer, who has 46 catches for 603 yards and seven touchdowns so far this season.

Nebraska has a decent stable of running backs to rely on, primarily Jamal Rule and Mekhi Nelson. So far this season, Rule has carried the ball 88 times for 632 yards and five touchdowns, while Nelson has 78 carries for 348 yards and five touchdowns.

Defensively, Nebraska is led in tackles by linebacker Owen Chambliss, while lineman Jahsear Whittington leads the Cornhuskers' pass rush with 4.5 sacks.

As stated before, Nebraska has a decent running game that will be matched up against a porous Rutgers defense that is particularly bad against the run. To make matters worse, the Knights will be extremely handicapped on offense with Duff out, as well as OL Kwabena Asamoah and starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan. Even backup quarterback AJ Surace is listed as questionable.

This game has the potential to unfold in a similar fashion to the last one for Rutgers, as both Nebraska and Wisconsin are very similar teams to one another. Questionable passing game, good running game, really good defense that can get pressure. However, it was Badger quarterback Ryan Hopkins who hit the Knights' defense for 241 yards and three touchdowns last week so it will be interesting to see what the Cornhuskers will do offensively following that performance.

Rutgers vs. Nebraska will kick off at 12:30 p.m. on Nov. 14 inside SHI Stadium. Live coverage will be available on the Big Ten Network.

articles.title: Holland Christian volleyball's revenge tour, stunning run ends in regional final
articles.summary: The Maroons earned revenge wins several times this month, but couldn't get one more in a loss to Grand Rapids Christian.
articles.body:
Best photos from Holland Christian vs Grand Rapids Christian regional final girls volleyball match

PLAINWELL - The stretch run of the season has been a revenge tour for the Maroons.

The Holland Christian volleyball team avenged a loss to Zeeland East to earn a share of the OK Black Conference title, avenged another to South Christian to win the Division 2 district title.

The next rematch was Grand Rapids Christian with a regional championship on the line.

The revenge tour ended there in a 25-18, 25-15, 25-19 loss to the Eagles in the Division 2 regional final on Thursday, Nov. 12, at Plainwell High School.

"I had a feeling that our season was going to go like that. We started a little slow and the girls rose to the occasion in a lot of intense moments. Their mental toughness in those moments is something I am beyond proud of," Holland Christian coach Kylie Leeuw said.

The Maroons started strong and hung on to a narrow lead early in the first set. But a huge kill down the middle by Sylvia Setsma by the Eagles, followed by a block then four HC errors turned the tables and put the Eagles up 14-8. The Eagles kept that momentum going and hung on to win the set 25-18.

In the second set, the Eagles pulled ahead with a couple of aces and strong serving, leading 19-14. Another ace and a 6-1 run to finish the set gave the Eagles the 25-15 win and a 2-0 lead.

Addi Meiste put down a couple of big kills in the third and Tessa Leeuw served up an ace to pull the Maroons within 18-14. Two more Leeuw kills made it 22-18 but after another ace, the Eagles hung on for the 25-19 win and the sweep.

The Eagles advanced to the state quarterfinals. The seniors have made the semis twice and are looking to finish with the ultimate high.

"We played our pace, which was important. We ran a fast offense and had really aggressive serving. Getting them out of system was huge," Grand Rapids Christian Coach Amy Huisken said. "It means so much for our seven seniors. It is a fantastic feeling. We are ready to go back and take it."

The Maroons will lose seniors Allison Lamer, Ella Terpstra and Mia Westerbeke. That leaves 12 from the postseason roster and most of the rotation who return, including hitters Addi Meiste and Tessa Leeuw as well as libero Kate Genzink, meaning this postseason run could be just the beginning for the young Maroons.

"Their attack is fast, powerful and all of the above. It was a speed we hadn't seen all year," Kylie Leeuw said. "We have some big shoes to fill with the ones leaving, but leaving on a high with how well we did is going to be big."

articles.title: Giants should embrace a rebuild as baseball heads into labor war, uncertainty
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants will never say they're in a rebuilding mode, but it seems like the perfect time for one as unknowns shroud what next season will loo...
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants just finished up what could be baseball's last major gathering in a very, very long time. The recently concluded general manager meetings in Las Vegas were the last official date on the baseball calendar before Dec. 1, which is when the current collective bargaining agreement expires and when the owners are expected to lockout the players.

What happens after that, and when baseball might resume, will be anybody's guess.

So how do the 97-loss Giants look heading into this great unknown? Like a team that's still trying to figure things out.

The Giants, along with all teams, face some urgency in the coming weeks as they try to assemble a roster before Dec. 1 that might resemble what they want their team to look like whenever baseball reopens its doors. There might be an abbreviated spring training, a shortened season - again, no one knows. But whenever baseball restarts, teams will want to be ready.

The Giants obviously have some big needs. Those 97 losses weren't a fluke. The most glaring are on the pitching staff: both starting pitching and bullpen relief (quickly shutting down Randy Rodriguez in the Arizona Fall League in his comeback attempt from Tommy John surgery was a reminder of just how much help they need).

Will the Giants make any significant moves in the next few weeks? Will they sacrifice any of their young prospects to make a deal? President of baseball operations Buster Posey said he's trying to pull off a balancing act.

"You're trying to thread the needle," he said, "of having the big league team in the spot they can win but also understanding that some of our top players in our system are probably two or three years away."

The Giants will never, ever, ever say they're in a rebuilding mode. But we'll say it: They should be in rebuilding mode. It seems like the perfect time. They're coming off a terrible season, one that only improved slightly and became a tad more interesting when the team - mostly due to injury - went younger. No one knows what next season will look like, but it may end up being truncated and weird. Seems like a perfect opportunity to rebuild and give those young prospects serious playing time.

Going young may also be better for manager Tony Vitello , whose background is as a college coach. Vitello also popped up in Las Vegas, part of his offseason of going hither and yon. He told reporters he's been on planes constantly since the season ended in late September. Much of his travel has involved returning to college: soaking in the Tennessee adulation at a Vols game in Knoxville, sporting a "Yee Haw Brewing" hat on the sidelines of a USC game next to Lincoln Riley. Up next, Baton Rouge, where he'll hang out with Lane Kiffin when LSU hosts Texas.

All these trips seem to underscore that Vitello is way more comfortable with the college scene than he is as a major league manager. But he indicated there's an ulterior motive to his trips. He's trying to learn different forms of leadership and he thinks "football coaches are the craziest human beings in the world." He went on to talk about how losing one football game is like the end of the world.

But that point only emphasized how completely different college football coaches and major league managers are: there might not be two more different head coaching jobs in all of big-time sports. College football coaches have a 12-game schedule. They're little dictators, controlling every aspect of their program. Managers have 162 games to navigate and, especially these days, are largely not in control of their personnel or the weightiest decisions. It requires a far more subtle touch.

One would think Vitello might be better off picking the brain of Dusty Baker or Bruce Bochy - or Natalie Nakase . After all, he was spotted wandering through the Valkyries victory parade. Instead he's tapping into Riley, a coach battling for his job, and Kiffin, one of the slimiest, most unethical coaches in all of sports. But, hey, they're probably fun trips.

The field of play wasn't the only place the Giants took an L this year. Principal owner Charles Johnson, the biggest sports donor in the last election cycle ($2.6 million) also took huge losses, as a result of the blue tsunami that swept the country on election day. He funneled money into Republican committees and candidates who were overwhelmingly rejected by the voters.

One Republican ousted from office was Cindy Hyde-Smith, who lost her Mississippi Senate seat to Scott Colom, the first Black Senator in the state since reconstruction. You might remember that Johnson and his wife contributed to Smith's special election in 2018, despite outrage over the tone-deaf politician saying that if another booster "invited me to a public hanging, I'd be in the front row." Johnson asked for his donation back after the outcry but it didn't stop him from gifting $500 to her campaign in August 2025.

That could be one more reason for the Giants to rebuild and go younger in this strange upcoming season. After dumping money into losing candidates, the principal owner might want to save some cash.

articles.title: Yordan Alvarez Takes Home American League MVP Award
articles.summary: The American League was full of elite talent in 2026, but the Yordan Alvarez MVP season stood head and shoulders above the rest. The Houston Astros star hitt...
articles.body:
The American League was full of elite talent in 2026, but the Yordan Alvarez MVP season stood head and shoulders above the rest. The Houston Astros star hitter secured the American League Most Valuable Player award in a competitive race. Runner-up Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays and third-place finisher Bobby Witt Jr. of the Kansas City Royals were the other finalists, and both were very deserving. However, Alvarez's hot bat made him an early-season MVP candidate , and he kept it going. Alvarez won the award unanimously, garnering all 30 first-place votes.

Alvarez has always been a good hitter, but in 2026 he took it to the next level. His power is obvious, but his contact skills were great this season. He hit. 316, which is the best in the league. He had 42 home runs, the fourth most in the league. It was second best in the AL, one behind Pete Alonso .

Alvarez added 106 RBI, tied for the fifth most in MLB. Once again, it was second in the AL behind Alonso. Alvarez had a commanding lead in OBP, with .432. The second-best was Colorado Rockies rookie TJ Rumfield with .390. He also led the league with a .601 slugging percentage, while Pete Crow-Armstrong was second with .570. This led to the best OPS, at 1.033. The second best was Crow-Armstrong with a .942 OPS.

Yordan Alvarez's MVP season wasn't defined by any defensive production, but his bat was elite. In most offensive categories, he ranked first in the league. If he wasn't, then he was in the top five. Nobody was better as an overall hitter, so Alvarez made a very convincing case as he helped the Astros squeak into the postseason .

Alvarez's MVP Award Joins Crowded Trophy Case

Yordan Alvarez's MVP Award is the highlight of his season, but it is far from the only recognition he received. Alvarez already had a great resume coming into 2026. In 2022, he was named to the All-MLB First Team and won a Silver Slugger. In 2022 and 2024, he was named the Astros Most Valuable Player. He is a four-time All-Star, making it every year since 2022, except 2025.

Alvarez has also won AL Player of the Month four times, AL Player of the Week six times, and been named to the All-MLB Second Team four times. In 2021, he won the ALCS MVP.

In his rookie season, he was a three-time AL Rookie of the Month. Alvarez was also named the Astros Rookie of the Year, MLB Players' Choice AL Outstanding Rookie, and the Jackie Robinson AL Rookie of the Year, along with countless Minor League Awards. This year, he was named as a finalist for a Silver Slugger, which is still yet to be announced.

The Astros have had many talented players in their history, but Yordan Alvarez's MVP award is the third in team history. Jeff Bagwell won it in 1994, when they were in the National League. In only 110 games, he had 39 home runs and 116 RBI. His .368 batting average was elite, making him a clear choice for MVP.

Then Jose Altuve won it in 2017. Altuve hit .346 with 32 stolen bases. He also had 24 home runs and 81 RBI. Altuve became the first AL MVP in the Astros franchise history. With the season he had, Yordan Alvarez MVP season more than deserved to join the history books .

Yordan Alvarez's MVP case was clear. He had one of the best bats in the league. It's hard to say there was anyone above him offensively. The combination of contact and power is rare. The season ended on a wrong note, as they were eliminated in the playoffs , but it does not take away from his MVP season.

His awards case was already full, so he needs to find more room to store the AL MVP Award. He has a resumé that most big leaguers could only ever dream of achieving. Not only that, but he also joined a short list of franchise icons. Alvarez is a star, but his 2026 season has cemented him as one of the best players in the entire league.
