articles.title: Yankees’ Cam Schlittler, Ben Rice finish fourth, ninth in AL MVP voting
articles.summary: Houston’s Yordan Alvarez took home the award, but the Yankees’ pair both placed high.
articles.body:
By virtue of them not being announced as finalists, we knew that neither Cam Schlittler or Ben Rice were going to win the 2026 American League Most Valuable Player Award. However, we had a pretty good feeling that the Cy Young and the slugger were going to finish high in the voting. On Thursday night, the announcement came , and Schlittler and Rice finished in fourth and ninth place respectively.

The Astros' Yordan Alvarez took home the award over fellow finalists Junior Caminero and Bobby Witt Jr. Alvarez ended up being the unanimous winner, receiving all 30 first place votes. Caminero was a clear second, receiving all but three second place votes.

One of the three second-place votes that didn't go to Caminero did go to Schlittler — shout out to Dave Skretta of the Associated Press. The rest of his votes range somewhere between third and 10th. He only just narrowly missed being named a finalist, as he finished only seven points behind Witt for third. While a pitcher winning MVP has happened in recent memory, it can often be hard for them to get close considering that they have an award for themselves in the Cy Young. Finishing fourth matches Shane Bieber in 2020 — although there's quite a big caveat on that one — for the best finish for a pure pitcher (sorry, Shohei) since Clayton Kershaw's National League win in 2014.

As for Rice, he received two third-place votes himself, but all the rest of his ranged between fifth and 10th place. I think if I were voting, I would've had him higher up in ninth, but I am somewhat biased in the fact that I watch him every day.

Those were the only two Yankees to receive votes, which isn't particularly shocking. You can view the full list here . For those curious, the Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong was unsurprisingly named the unanimous winner in the NL.

There were certainly plenty of aspects to the Yankees' 2026 season that were disappointing, but Schlittler and Rice certainly weren't the reasons.

articles.title: Izzo Still Isn’t Satisfied at Center After Duke Win
articles.summary: Michigan State is 3-0 after beating Duke, and Izzo still is not sold on one position. #Spartans
articles.body:
Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo met with the media Thursday ahead of the Spartans' game against Northern Iowa , and even after beating Duke 79-73 two nights earlier he went right back to the same sore spot. In a video posted by SpartanMag , Izzo called the center position his team's biggest weakness, then went through the rotation of Anton Bonke, Jesse McCulloch and Ethan Taylor one by one.

"Still our weakness is the center position. You know, Anton (Bonke) is probably doing more than we give him credit for. He's averaging seven rebounds a game in 15 minutes of play, which is phenomenal. Did a better job on the ball screens," Izzo said. "Jesse (McCulloch) is doing more and more. You know, he gives us the pick and pop ability. He's doing more and more. But Ethan (Taylor) probably has the most overall length, size, athleticism, and talent, and we're going to get it out of him, and it's gonna take a little time."

Tom Izzo Says Ethan Taylor Gets In His Own Way

Taylor is averaging 12 minutes off the bench in the Spartans' first three games but has flashed solid play in the limited time. He is averaging 4.7 points and three rebounds a game while shooting 80% from the field. Against Duke, Taylor had five points in just eight minutes of action, limited by foul trouble. Izzo thinks the main thing holding him back is his own head.

"Ethan's (Taylor) gonna be a really good player if he can get out of his own way right now. You know, he gets down on himself. He doesn't get down on us. He gets down on himself, and yet makes some good plays," Izzo said. "He's got the quickness to be able to cover ball screens, he's got the strength, he's 255, he's intelligent, he's got all the things going for him except, I'd say, his biggest negative is he struggles on how to take coaching, but he also struggles on how to approach things himself."

Not Every Player Is Held To The Same Standard

In the first week of games, the Spartans ran past Quinnipiac 96-59 and Toledo 91-61, and Izzo still was not satisfied. He said he was not happy with a lot of his players last week and went looking for individual conversations, telling forward Coen Carr to be more aggressive and pushing guard Jeremy Fears Jr. to play better rather than just well. Then he explained why the bar is not the same for everyone.

"Some guys have to be held to a higher standard than others. Some guys get paid more than others, so it works both ways," Izzo said. "So everybody's not treated quite equally, and we put a little more pressure on our key guys last week, meetings, practice, individual meetings, and I like the fact that they responded, just every one of them did."

Jeremy Fears Jr. And Coen Carr Answered Against Duke

In the first two games of the season, Fears Jr. had seven turnovers and struggled to draw fouls, getting to the free throw line only 10 times. Against Duke he still had four turnovers, but he made up for it as a foul magnet, getting to the line 17 times and making 12. Carr played only 17 minutes and picked up two fouls, but he scored nine points on five shots.

Jordan Scott Was The Team's Defensive Leader

Izzo also praised forward Jordan Scott, who carried the defense against Duke. Scott had six blocks, six of Michigan State's eight on the night, and led the team with nine rebounds. He has struggled on offense so far, shooting 41.4% from the field and 26.7% from three , but he has made up for it with smart play. Izzo wants that kind of defense to keep showing up, and he said it is a matter of wanting it, not of talent.

"Too many people, the stat people, the analytics people, you know, they don't go on those kind of plays, and those kind of plays win for you. Can you maintain that?" Izzo said. "It's really more about your energy, your desire, your willing to do it. It's a will thing, not a skill thing."

articles.title: Blue Jays apologize for Anthony Santander's posts, condemn Islamophobia
articles.summary: After receiving criticism for a weak response, the Toronto Blue Jays condemned Islamophobia and apologized for Anthony Santander's Instagram posts.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays have apologized for Anthony Santander's Islamophobic Instagram posts that criticized U.S. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed .

On Thursday, Nov. 12, the club posted a statement attributed to President and CEO Mark Shapiro to their social media channels. Toronto said it had conversations with members of the city's Muslim community to reflect on the incident, which happened after national elections in the United States.

"The Blue Jays are deeply sorry to the Muslim community and our fans for the pain and harm these Islamophobic posts have caused," the statement said. "We will work with leaders in Muslim communities to fight against all forms of hate."

The statement continued by saying the incident was an "opportunity to listen and learn" that "reaffirms our beliefs and values as an organization."

"We condemn Islamophobia and all forms of hate."

Two days earlier, at the General Managers Meetings in Las Vegas, Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins expressed concern over the right fielder's actions.

"There really aren't words to express my level of disappointment with him making those comments. I've expressed that to him," he said, according to Sportsnet reporter Ben Nicholson-Smith , "... anything exacerbating some level of anti-Islamic hate is just extremely concerning, extremely disappointing."

The official apology comes after the club released a previous response to Santander's Instagram stories that criticized El-Sayed, who won a highly contested race for U.S. Senator in Michigan and in doing so became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. Screenshots of a video showed a caption that read, "America voted for Sharia (law) last night!" Another post seen in screenshots had a caption on the video that said, "Islam is not peaceful."

"Baseball is for everyone," said the initial statement, which was attributed to a team spokesperson, "and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."

The previous response received criticism for not apologizing and not taking a strong enough stance against Islamophobia.

The 32-year-old did not play for Toronto last season as the Blue Jays went 79-83 and failed to make the playoffs. He has been struggling with shoulder injuries and had surgery in February.

The Venezuela native was limited to just 54 regular season games in 2025, the first year of a five-year, $92.5 million contract, due to a left shoulder subluxation. He returned in time to play in five playoff games, but a back injury forced his removal from the ALCS roster, ending his season. The Blue Jays made it to the World Series, where they lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers in seven games.

articles.title: David Guetta, John Summit to headline free CFP music festival in Las Vegas
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS — David Guetta and John Summit will headline two nights of free concerts at Grand Prix Plaza in January as Las Vegas hosts the College Football Pla...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — David Guetta and John Summit will headline two nights of free concerts at Grand Prix Plaza in January as Las Vegas hosts the College Football Playoff national championship.

The College Football Playoff announced a 10-act lineup for AT&T Playoff Playlist Live, with five acts performing each night Jan. 23-24, 2027. The all-ages festival will take place at 4400 Koval Lane ahead of the national championship game Monday, Jan. 25, at Allegiant Stadium. Gates open at 3 p.m. each day. Registration will be limited, with details to be announced through the CFP's official mobile app.

Guetta will headline Saturday's lineup, which also features Marshmello, Alison Wonderland, HoneyLuv and Girl Math. The two-time Grammy winner's hits include "Titanium" with Sia and "I'm Good (Blue)" with Bebe Rexha. Marshmello's collaborations span pop and country, including "Numb" with Khalid and "Miles on It" with Kane Brown. Alison Wonderland incorporates live vocals and cello into her sets, while HoneyLuv brings a house and tech-house sound and Girl Math blends punk and dance music.

"I've had the chance to perform at some incredible events and in front of some amazing crowds throughout my career, but this is something completely new for me," Guetta said in a statement.

Summit tops Sunday's bill, which also includes FISHER, SOFI TUKKER, Korolova and Skilah. Summit, the Chicago-born DJ and producer behind "Where You Are" and "Go Back," has sold out shows at Madison Square Garden and the Kia Forum. FISHER earned a Grammy nomination for his breakout track "Losing It," and SOFI TUKKER, the duo of Sophie Hawley-Weld and Tucker Halpern, earned nominations for its debut single "Drinkee" and its album "Treehouse."

"The CFP experience on South Beach was so electric last year, and I can't wait to run it back for all the fans in Las Vegas," Summit said in a statement.

Las Vegas emcee Robert "Bojo" Ackah and ESPN studio host Alexis Nunes will host both nights, with Las Vegas DJ Joe Green playing between sets.

Championship festivities begin Friday, Jan. 22, with Dr Pepper CFP Fan Central at the Las Vegas Convention Center's West Hall. The free event runs through Sunday and will feature interactive games, pep rallies, autograph signings and the CFP's inaugural flag football showcase. Fans can also attend Saturday's media day, when players and coaches from both championship teams will meet with reporters in separate one-hour sessions.

The CFP Foundation will hold its Extra Yard for Teachers Summit on Saturday at the Bellagio's "O" Theater. The free event is open to registration and will feature speakers, classroom resource giveaways and a reception for educators.

Sunday's CFP Trophy Trot will feature 5K and 10K races along the Las Vegas Strip, along with a one-mile fun run. Participants will receive a shirt and a finisher's medal and will have opportunities to win tickets to the championship game. The Taste of the CFP, also scheduled for Sunday, will feature food from Las Vegas-area chefs and a performance by the funk duo Tuxedo at Soleia Beach at The Vanderpump Las Vegas Hotel. Proceeds will benefit the CFP Foundation's Extra Yard for Teachers initiative.

On game day, the Allstate Championship Tailgate will open at 10 a.m. in the lots north of Allegiant Stadium. The event is included with a national championship game ticket and will feature performances by both teams' marching bands, live ESPN broadcasts and interactive games.

articles.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong is one of the greatest NL MVPs in history. Here's why.
articles.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong hit 45 home runs with 41 steals in his 2026 MVP season.
articles.body:
Pete Crow-Armstrong didn't just earn National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2026. He also put together one of the greatest MVP seasons the league has seen in the past half-century.

PCA swept to NL MVP honors in unanimous fashion, earning all 30 first-place votes in balloting released Thursday, Nov. 12 by the Baseball Writers' Association of America. The coronation seemed a formality, as "MVP!" chants grew louder in Wrigley Field and anywhere the Cubs took their five-tool center fielder on the road.

And by season's end, it was almost unfathomable what this 6-foot, 184-pound center fielder produced.

He led the major leagues with 45 home runs – and also topped every fielder at every position with 26 outs above average.

He led the NL with a .570 slugging percentage and .943 OPS - and also stole 41 bases in 48 attempts, becoming the seventh member of baseball's 40-40 club.

Major League Baseball's MVP winners since 2000

He led the majors with 119 runs scored as the leadoff man for an 89-win club, and his adjusted OPS was 56% higher than league average.

Add it all up, and Crow-Armstrong produced a major league-leading 9.8 WAR, as calculated by Baseball-Reference.

That's the most impactful NL MVP season, by that metric, since Barry Bonds accrued 10.6 WAR in 2004, the third time in four years he produced double-digits in that category. Before Bonds, Colorado's Larry Walker posted a 9.8 WAR, equal to PCA, in winning the 1997 MVP.

And to find a superior MVP season not moored in the high era of baseball's performance-enhancing drug scandal or played at altitude (though WAR partially bakes that in), we have to go back to Bonds in 1993 (9.9) and Joe Morgan way back in 1975, when he posted 11 WAR on the strength of a .466 OBP and 67 steals.

At 24 years old, PCA stands shoulder to shoulder with those greats.

It's been a meteoric rise, from 19th overall pick by the New York Mets , to his 2021 trade to the Cubs in exchange for Javier Báez, to his year-over-year gains in less sexy but crucial categories like contact and walk rate, all of which have coalesced to make him arguably the game's best all-around everyday player.

And now, National League MVP, perhaps the first of more to come.

articles.title: Rams place WR Puka Nacua on IR
articles.summary: Nacua injured the MCL and PCL in his knee and has turf toe.
articles.body:
A day after Sean McVay said the Rams wouldn't place Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the wide receiver went on IR.

McVay said "roster semantics" would keep Nacua on the 53-man roster, with every team getting only eight designated-to-return slots during the season. The Rams have used three of their designations and have Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson and now Nacua on IR with hopes of returning.

But with Nacua set to miss "extended time," as McVay said Wednesday, with MCL and PCL sprains in his knee and turf toe, the Rams opted to move him to the IR list.

Nacua will miss at least the next four games, with the Cowboys game on Dec. 20 the earliest he can return by rule.

The Rams signed wide receiver Brennan Presley to take Nacua's roster spot and added wide receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad.

articles.title: 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins hits back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja’s claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them “100% wrong” and “utter nonsense”...
articles.body:
Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense".

In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town.

Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility.

But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong.

"I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening.

"He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense."

Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January.

Khawaja was in the Australia XI when Cummins made his Test debut in 2011 and the pair were also once team-mates in domestic cricket with New South Wales.

"Usman is a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," said Cummins.

"In his book he's been casual with my life and the lives of many others - and, I think, Australian cricket.

"I support him to tell his story, 100%, I'm glad he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do."

In a media conference he arranged himself, Cummins began by promising to answer all questions because, he said: "I don't want to talk about this again after today."

At times emotional, Cummins addressed a wide range of topics, including:

Advice that some of Khawaja's claims are defamatory, but he will not take legal action

He had been in contact with Khawaja and Smith since the book was published, but not Warner

His belief that the one-year bans handed to Smith and Warner, and a nine-month suspension to Bancroft were "heavy handed"

He had no recollection of Australia tampering with the ball in the 2017-18 Ashes series against England

He had met with Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who has reviewed the files from the original investigation

Explaining why sandpaper would have been present in the dressing room and that it was sometimes used by bowlers in training in order to practise with a reverse-swinging ball

Khawaja's allegations have reopened the debate about the sandpaper plot, the investigation into the cheating, the culture of Australian cricket and the reputations of those involved.

The story has dominated the media in Australia and caused headlines around the cricketing world.

Khawaja has been supported by Warner and Chadd Sayers, a seam bowler who was part of the Australia squad on the 2018 tour of South Africa.

However, his allegations have been rejected by Darren Lehmann, who was then the Australia head coach and former England batter Graeme Hick, one of Lehmann's assistants. Mitchell Starc, another bowler on the tour, has also denied Khawaja's claims.

Khawaja has put a spotlight on Cummins and his fellow bowlers Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four were Australia's attack in Cape Town and remain their first-choice bowlers eight years later.

The quartet have always denied any knowledge of the plot, including in the release of a joint-statement in 2021.

In his book - Sabr - Khawaja alleged Australia were urged to find ways of getting the ball to swing by a coach, while Bancroft was later encouraged to cheat.

Khawaja also said he asked for the entire team to take responsibility for the controversy in Cape Town, but his request was rejected by two unnamed players.

Cummins said he does not recall any suggestion that the team should have shared the responsibility, or that it was rejected.

On the idea that the whole team were aligned in a plot to tamper with the ball, he said: "There was no masterplan around using illegal methods. People assume you've gone from very legal methods to suddenly taking sandpaper, and there must have been some huge masterplan.

"That is not the case. There's no grand plan. There's no team meeting. There's no bowlers saying this is what must happen."

"There's big leaps where Usman is being vague."

In his book, Khawaja detailed how he was not interviewed as part of the investigation despite sitting next to Bancroft in the changing rooms during the Test at Newlands.

Both Khawaja and Warner have criticised the investigation, which Greenberg has said he will not reopen.

Cummins confirmed he has met with Greenberg and, although the captain said he did not want to break a "confidence", that Greenberg has reviewed the sandpaper files since the release of Khawaja's book and found the accounts in the investigation to be "consistent".

Cummins has played 77 Tests for Australia and has been captain sine 2021. He said he has seen only one instance of ball-tampering in his career, during a domestic Sheffield Shield match, when a player took a bottletop on to the field.

However, he did admit that balls can sometimes be altered during training sessions, if bowlers want to practise in a certain way, or batters want to face a ball of a particular condition.

Cummins said it was not unknown for training balls to be scuffed in such circumstances, using sandpaper or even a Stanley knife.

When it was put to Cummins that he, as a bowler, must have suspected that the Cape Town ball had been tampered with, the 33-year-old described that bowlers often touch a ball as little as possible, in order to keep it dry and in a state where it will reverse-swing.

At the time of the sandpaper scandal, Cummins was 24 and playing in his 13th Test. Asked about a potential culture of ball-tampering in that era, Cummins said he noticed things then that he now realises could have been cheating.

On why Khawaja has chosen to speak now, at the end of his career, rather than in the intervening eight years, Cummins said the episode could have "weighed heavy" on the left-hander.

Addressing the culture of the Australia team eight years ago, Cummins said: "I didn't like the way we spoke to umpires, the opposition. I think there was a bit of an arrogance and a bit of an ugliness at times that didn't sit well with me as a young guy.

"Now I'm captain, I have spent a lot of time making sure that that's not the case."

Analysis - Cummins did not dodge a single question

Khawaja's claims - in his book, in interviews and on social media - have re-opened old wounds in Australian cricket, drawing battlelines that have verged on civil war.

Over the past few days, constant questions have been asked of who knew what and if the truth has been covered up in the intervening eight years.

The most pressure has been on the bowlers who played for Australia in Cape Town, - none more so than Cummins, given his rise to the captaincy.

He has been urged to front up, to show leadership. In a remarkable news conference in an indoor cricket centre in Sydney, Cummins did just that.

Others connected to the scandal who have faced the media in the past few days – Lehmann, Starc and Mitchell Marsh – have almost implicated themselves with vague responses to straight questions. Not Cummins.

The captain did not duck or dodge any of the subjects that were thrown at him by a huge throng of assembled journalists. He did so without any intervention from a media manager.

What was most striking was his criticism of Khawaja, once a team-mate and friend. In being so forceful of his rejection of what Khawaja has claimed, Cummins appeared to be a reliable witness.

The question is whether this will be enough to end the speculation. Khawaja is sure to have another say. So too Warner, who is yet to release a book of his own.

Cummins cannot prove a negative, so can use only his words when it comes to convincing the world he was not involved in the sandpaper plot.

On this occasion, Cummins was impressive. Still, when he says he never wants to talk about sandpaper again, that feels like wishful thinking.

articles.title: 4 OU players to watch this week against Ole Miss
articles.summary: 4 players to watch when the Oklahoma Sooners host the Ole Miss Rebels.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners will see a lot of the Ole Miss Rebels over the next few years in the SEC, as the league has deemed the two teams annual rivals for the next four seasons, starting this year. Combine that with the Sooners and the Rebels already facing off in OU's first two SEC seasons, and the two programs with virtually no shared history are going to get very familiar with each other.

Oklahoma is 0-3 against Ole Miss, and the next chance to win comes this week, as the Sooners return home to Norman. OU got a cathartic road win over Florida last week, while Ole Miss was dominated at home by Georgia last week. Two teams with very different mindsets will meet on Owen Field on Saturday afternoon.

After the unexpected victory, the Sooners will lean on some key players to try to win two games in a row for the first time since November of 2025. As always with OU, injury concerns will force certain players to step up and help the program make a bowl game with a win this week.

Here are four players to watch for the Sooners against the Rebels.

With interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten at the controls, several pass-catchers saw an expanded role in OU's victory in "The Swamp." That included the tight ends, where Rocky Beers leads the way. With his position coach and one of the greatest TEs ever to play dialing up the offense, it's safe to assume Beers will be targeted a lot against the Rebels.

OU's passing game options are as healthy right now as they've been all season. Beers has been an important part of the passing attack all season long, and he's somebody that is clearly trusted to get open and make important catches at important moments. In a game where the offense will have to produce more than it did last week, Beers could play a huge role.

Oklahoma made more of a commitment to the running game against Florida, shortening the game by bleeding the clock and keeping the ball on the ground and out of harm's way. As well as it worked against the Gators, it's hard to see Witten going away from it to start this game. With fellow running back Tory Blaylock's status up in the air for Saturday, it could mean an increased workload for OU's top RB, Lloyd Avant.

The Sooners seem to have settled on a starting offensive line of Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Jake Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris, and that group being healthy and working together is good news for any OU ball carrier. Avant continues to get the most opportunities of any Sooner running back, and if Blaylock can't play, he could get more totes or still split carries with Jonathan Hatton Jr.

Linebackers Kip Lewis and Owen Heinecke are playing their penultimate games on Owen Field, and they are two of the most special players of the Brent Venables era in Norman. They struggled in the South Carolina loss, but played very well in the Florida win. Facing another dynamic dual-threat quarterback in Trinidad Chambliss this week, all eyes will be on how well the inside linebacker duo handles his playmaking.

Additionally, both of the next men up at inside LB, Cole Sullivan and James Nesta, are not guaranteed to play against Ole Miss, so Lewis and Heinecke may have to go the distance again this week against the Rebels. It's not ideal, but if any two players on OU's roster can handle it, it's these two.

Oklahoma's secondary has been banged up in recent weeks, but it's getting healthier, led by defensive back Peyton Bowen. He was limited in the Florida win, but he should be fully healthy this week, which is a massive boost for the Sooners. His younger brother, Eli Bowen, was back in the lineup against the Gators as well, and OU might have its full complement of starters in the secondary healthy for the first time in a long time this week.

Jacobe Johnson may also be back for the first time in weeks, which would give the Sooners more depth behind its starting cornerbacks. The Rebels have a strong passing attack that has become the strength of their offense without running back Kewan Lacy in the lineup, so Bowen, the veteran leader of the secondary, will be tasked with making sure his guys are in the right places against the wide-open Rebel attack.

articles.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
articles.summary: Oregon State's explosive passing offense, led by nation-leading receiver Jesse Legree, faces a Washington State defense that prides itself on preventing big...
articles.body:
CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State's outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive.

The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU's 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week's matchup with Washington State.

"You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times," Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. "I think it's about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he's at."

The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage.

WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season.

"We don't want to let the verticals up," Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. "We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first."

WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree.

OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays.

"People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage," Dahlen said. "They're going to try and two-hand jam. If they're going to try and two-hand jam, it's like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can't do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can't do it that way.

"That's what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can't just put a safety over the top of him because if he's in the backfield, what are you going to do there?"

Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week.

Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They're confident they can challenge any defense vertically.

"The underneath throws are going to be there," Hampton said. "We got the best OC in the country; we're going to be able to go deep if we want to."
